direction: Promote the obstruction atlas as the single champion object.
rationale: It is the only route that naturally bridges lower-bound search, upper-bound lemmas, and proof reuse.
first_step: Build the parent/extension/failure-core schema and score recurrence on the initial frontier set.
expected_signal: A small number of canonical cores cover a nontrivial fraction of failed extensions across multiple parent families.

direction: Keep H2 strictly as a decomposition audit, not a second main project.
rationale: It is too close to the current upper-bound literature to justify early budget.
first_step: Benchmark pair-split and shell primitives on solved ladder rungs under matched proof logging.
expected_signal: Residue size and proof bytes improve simultaneously relative to split/gluing.

direction: Use certificate-carrying artifacts as an attachment layer only.
rationale: Proof infrastructure alone does not move the bound, but it can stabilize H1/H2 gains.
first_step: Attach proof-format stubs and checker-time accounting to the top recurring obstruction cores.
expected_signal: Some learned or mined cores survive held-out reuse with acceptable checker cost.

direction: Retain rare-event sampling only as a data-diversification sidecar.
rationale: The falsifier memo already kills optimizer-only novelty claims in this area.
first_step: Compare obstruction diversity harvested from rare-event near-misses against atlas-only failures.
expected_signal: New core families appear without becoming a proxy-metric story.
